account:
Today my ordinary mayoral schedule continues, but there are hints of activity I have not been told about. Several townspeople have repeated a claim about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk 11 said baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour were there, and reported builder carrying a sack of bread at the bakery and square_north_1. These are reports, not events I personally witnessed. The repeated wording may simply be gossip; I have no confirmed proposal or explanation. Bread being carried in quantity could be provisions for a gathering or work, but that is only a possibility.

My ten o'clock mill inspection had no identifiable host or grain report. Secretary attended but did not know who originally arranged it, and offered to inquire at the bakery. I went there and did not find baker. The account ledgers also remain unavailable, despite my requests; I cannot yet connect that to the rumours. My office record had no new preparatory papers this morning.

An unusual definite arrangement is my eighteen-hundred appointment with innkeeper in the great hall, with an explicit request not to arrive early. I approved that appointment, but its purpose has not been explained. Freight has also been checking the hall schedule. Together with the reported involvement of innkeeper and neighbour and builder's bread sack, this could indicate preparations for a gathering, perhaps a surprise, rather than an actual bridge or port project. I do not know yet and should not treat that guess as fact.

I kept lunch at home and have now returned to town hall for the thirteen-hundred council letters. Tea with neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage is at fifteen, office time at sixteen-thirty, and the great-hall appointment at eighteen. I intend to keep these appointments and seek firsthand explanations without arriving early for the hall meeting.
